# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination

**RE: Appeal of Denial – Partial Knee Replacement (CPT 27446)**
**Member:** Casey Iverson
**Member ID:** W207784190
**Payer/Plan:** Fidelis Care (Commercial/ACA), New York
**Denial Date:** 2026-08-25
**Reference Number:** POC-1ACF427871-17933
**Governing Policy:** 2026 Evolent Clinical Guidelines – Musculoskeletal Surgery ([https://www1.radmd.com/sites/default/files/2026-05/2026%20Evolent%20Musculoskeletal%20Surgery%20Guidelines.pdf](https://www1.radmd.com/sites/default/files/2026-05/2026%20Evolent%20Musculoskeletal%20Surgery%20Guidelines.pdf))

Dear Fidelis Care Appeals Department,

I am writing to appeal the denial of my partial knee replacement (CPT 27446), which I received notice of on 2026-08-25. I am asking that this decision be reconsidered. My surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I believe the record supports that conclusion.

## Why I am appealing

The denial notice states that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." I want to explain, in plain terms, why I believe that conclusion does not match what is in my chart.

I should be transparent about one thing: the plan document I was able to review, the 2026 Evolent Clinical Guidelines – Musculoskeletal Surgery, is the governing policy named in my denial's applicable medical policy reference. However, the specific criteria language I have access to from that guideline concerns cervical spine fusion procedures (such as ACDF and posterior cervical decompression with fusion), not partial knee replacement. Because that language does not apply to a knee procedure, I am not quoting it here — I don't want to attribute policy language to my case that does not actually govern it. I am asking Fidelis Care to identify and apply the specific criteria that its guidelines set out for partial knee replacement, and I am providing the clinical evidence below so that comparison can be made directly.

## The clinical evidence in my record

My chart contains the following, which I believe supports the medical necessity of this surgery:

- **Imaging:** An MRI of my knee on 2026-07-30 showed full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition, and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 changes medially. This is significant, objective imaging evidence of advanced joint disease.
- **Duration and progression of symptoms:** I have had progressive knee pain for 24 months that has not been relieved by rest.
- **Conservative treatment already completed:**
  - Supervised physical therapy focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion — 8 weeks, 16 visits, from 2026-05-14 to 2026-07-09, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note.
  - NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief.
  - A corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-03, which gave only about 4 weeks of partial relief.
- **Functional impact:** I cannot climb stairs without assistance, and I wake 3–4 times nightly because of pain.
- **Exam findings:** My physical exam showed positive provocative testing on the affected knee, and my range of motion is limited by pain.
- **No contraindications noted:** There is no active infection or untreated substance use documented, my BMI is 29, and I am a non-smoker.

Taken together, I believe this record shows both objective imaging confirmation of severe, end-stage joint damage and a documented, adequate trial of conservative treatment that did not resolve my symptoms. My surgeon has reviewed this history and recommended partial knee replacement as medically necessary.

## What I am asking

I am asking Fidelis Care to reconsider this denial in light of the imaging findings and treatment history above, and to apply the specific plan criteria that actually govern partial knee replacement (CPT 27446) to my case. If there are additional records or clarifications that would help with this review, please let me know what is needed and I will work with my surgeon's office to provide it.

I understand my appeal must be received by 2027-02-21. I am submitting this appeal using the address printed on my denial notice, and I understand I can also check ambetterhealth.com or call the number on my member ID card for my state's appeal form if needed.

Thank you for reconsidering my case.

Sincerely,

**Casey Iverson**
Member ID: W207784190
[Address]
[Phone number]
[Email address]
[Date of signature]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*

○ Upper extremity weakness ○ Unsteady gait related to myelopathy/balance or generalized lower extremity weakness ○ Disturbance with coordination ○ Hyperreflexia ○ Hoffmann sign ○ Positive Babinski sign and/or clonus ● Progressive neurological deficit (motor deficit, bowel or bladder dysfunction) with corresponding evidence of spinal cord or nerve root compression on an MRI or CT scan images – immediate surgical evaluation is indicated When ALL of the following criteria are met (6–8):

● Cervical radiculopathy or myelopathy due to ruptured disc, spondylosis, spinal instability, or deformity ● Failure of conservative treatment* for a minimum of six (6) weeks within the last six (6) months;
